method: SUBJECT (a phase served locally | staged diff | branch or PR | a real-test claim to be checked instead of trusted | production with no diff) x ARRIVAL (explicit | implicit | contextual). Positives include the symptoms the description names — a verdict proved against the fixed line only, a new branch never exercised, a test that touched only a mock, a verdict older than the latest edit, an attack designed by the author — plus the two modes 4.0.0 adds: per-phase local against the phase DoD, and the production check from the repo's real_test journey, with the logged-in-profile rule (never a password). Negatives: tdd-dev, review, ship, a docs-only change, a folder with no git.

cases.prompt: Real-test this staged diff before I commit: derive the perimeter from the change itself, not from memory.
I fixed the newline collapse. Before this goes anywhere, check that the branch I actually added is exercised and not just the line I edited.
Last time we validated against the function that had already been replaced and it sat broken in prod for three days. Don't let that happen here.
Give me a merge-readiness verdict on PR #901: MERGEABLE, MERGEABLE-CON-GAP or NOT-MERGEABLE, with the matrix per file.
Deploy this branch to staging and actually interrogate it — the endpoints the diff crosses, the row in the DB, the provider trace — not the home page.
Everything is green but every green test here mocks the database and the LLM. I don't believe it.
Someone left a verdict saying this is mergeable. Check the claim instead of trusting it — the tree has moved since.
Try to break this change every way you can before we merge it, and don't let the person who wrote it design the attempts.
Write the failing test for this acceptance criterion first, prove its red, then implement the minimum that makes it pass.
Read this diff for naming, structure and whether it follows our conventions, and rank what you find by severity.
Merge the approved PR, deploy it, and watch the canary against the baseline.
I fixed a typo in the README. Do I need to spin up the whole stack for this?
This folder is not under version control at all — there is no commit to hash. Review it by hand.
Phase 3 changes what the quote page shows. Run it locally against the phase DoD before I close the phase; no staging.
Testa l'app: fai il giro del cliente in produzione col profilo di prova e dimmi se qualcosa si è rotto.
Attack this decision record from fresh context before the founder accepts it.
